sections.title: Identity and form
sections.text: The catalogue's Capsicum entry depicts Capsicum annuum, including a bell-pepper type, rather than the whole genus. It is a cultivated herb or subshrub bearing white flowers and fleshy berries. Fruit size, shape, colour and pungency vary greatly among cultivars.

sections.title: Food and image
sections.text: The berries are eaten raw or cooked. Hot forms contain capsaicin, which irritates the mouth and eyes; the red, blocky fruit in the plate is one sweet-pepper form and is not representative of every C. annuum.

sections.title: Related pepper
sections.text: Capsicum pubescens is an Andean pepper with hairy leaves, purple flowers and dark seeds, unlike the white-flowered bell-pepper form shown here.
